facts.statement: The genus Symmorium was described by Edward Drinker Cope in 1893.
Symmorium lived during the Devonian and Carboniferous periods in the United States and Russia.
facts.quote: Symmorium is an extinct symmoriiform cartilaginous fish from the Devonian and Carboniferous of the United States (Illinois) and Russia.

facts.statement: Symmorium looked similar to Stethacanthus in size and appearance but lacked the spine-brush complex found on the first dorsal fin.
facts.quote: Symmorium bears close similarity in size and appearance to Stethacanthus but lacks the "spine-brush complex" in place of the first dorsal fin.

facts.statement: Scientists debate whether Symmorium and Stethacanthus represent male and female forms of the same species or distinct genera.
facts.quote: Some paleontologists think that the two forms represented the males and females of related species, while other scientists think they were distinct genera.

facts.statement: Some scientists hypothesize that Symmorium was the female form of Stethacanthus.
facts.quote: Los científicos consideran que Symmorium era la hembra de Stethacanthus.

facts.statement: Symmorium is classified within the family Stethacanthidae.
Symmorium fossils date from the Famennian to the Gzhelian stages, between 372.15 and 298.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Famennian to Gzhelian (372.15 to 298.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The type species Symmorium reniforme was named by Edward Drinker Cope in 1893.
rejected.quote: The type species, Symmorium reniforme, was named by Edward Drinker Cope in 1893
